notes: This is one corrected typescript page. The upper handwritten page number is 4; the lower-left archive pencil number is also 4. They were inspected and inventoried separately. H’s page{4} already carries matching metadata, so no number-omission difference was invented. There is no written date, letterhead, signature, or page total on this scan.

The whole page was viewed once for layout, followed by half a once and half b once in that order. The halves were read line by line against both supplied witnesses, including their agreements. Twenty-two tight crops were then made only for loci left open by those half views, and each crop was inspected once. No whole half was enlarged or reopened; no settled locus was recropped. The image metadata reads were only for dimensions and crop coordinates. No OCR, text-recognition output, PDF text layer, web source, other scan, other reader output, or delegation was used.

The start timestamp is the first clock observation, made after reading the brief and supplied textual packet; the recorded view times are clock observations returned just after each view or crop-view batch, rather than invented per-image timing estimates.

Coverage: every text block, every word ending and visible punctuation mark, both quoted spans, all inline and displayed formulae, all indices and exponents, alphabet choices, relation and arrow forms, cancellations, additions, hooks, underlines and both numberings were compared with both C and H. This includes the agreed expressions X in Ob C, X tensor X, s(X), pi_1(C)=Aut(1_C), the three left-subscript-2 torsion expressions, 2x=0, the repeated s map, all pi pairs, both K expressions, every H expression, i not equal to 0,1, X in S, F(X), and S inverse C. This coverage is visual verification, not a mathematical proof check.

The page states that the symmetry of X tensor X produces a canonical homomorphism s from pi_0 to the 2-torsion subgroup of pi_1. It states a classification of Picard categories by the two commutative groups and s, with non-canonical equivalence explicitly inserted. It identifies vanishing s with strictness and invokes an empty reference placeholder for the strict case. These are statements transcribed from the page; no theorem was independently established in this reading.

The Remarques passage interprets strict Picard categories through a full subcategory of the derived category of (Ab), with a displayed-in-line homology vanishing condition outside 0 and 1. The visible corrections move the degree marks from the superior positions to inferior positions and exchange the two later H degrees. The old superior i/1 remains uncertain. The crop establishes positions and strokes, not the validity of the claimed categorical interpretation.

The phrase non unique ! includes the handwritten exclamation point inside the parentheses. The subsequent prospective sentences say Il y aurait lieu and encore dans les limbes, then devraient être un jour … étudiés dans le cadre des champs.
